text:
Anton Lundell missed a game last weekend, day to day, and came back to the kind of week Florida needed: two assists against Columbus, then two goals against Detroit on Thursday. Add the hat trick he scored on eight shots against Winnipeg on Oct. 30, and the two-time Cup winner has 6 goals in 19 games, 5 of them in his last ten.

The scoring line still undersells him. Florida is taking 59% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 8.4 points better than without him, and his own chances are up to 1.15 expected goals per 60 from 0.89 last season. His shooting is normal. What isn't normal is his teammates' finishing: the Panthers have scored 6.9 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there, which explains why he has only 4 assists. That kind of gap usually swings back.

Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming on the power play, yet he has just one power-play point so far. Watch that number, and the assists; both have room to grow without him changing a thing.
